summary.text: 用 is traditionally analyzed as a picture of a handled container, though the surviving evidence does not settle its original referent. Oracle-bone examples attest it in ‘carry out/use’ contexts; the proposed link from container to that use is a borrowing account whose sound match is unverified.

formation.text: Pictographic under the reported bucket-and-handle analysis: the whole graph is interpreted as a container, with the body on the left and handle on the right. This conflicts with the received 說文 analysis, which parses it as 卜 and 中. A separate account links 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, while another parses it as 同 plus a handle and treats 同 as phonetic. The evidence here does not resolve these competing analyses; no phonetic component is established.

components.text: The whole pictographic graph is interpreted as a bucket or container: its left side is read as the body and its right side as a handle. The proposed referent is an attributed paleographic interpretation; no facsimile was independently inspected.

history.text: A character-form catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script, and 說文 forms of 用. Its accessible text does not describe their individual strokes or establish a detailed graphic sequence, so these categories should not be read as proof of specific shape changes.

The reported bucket-and-handle interpretation conflicts with the received 說文 structural account 從卜從中. Another report treats 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, whereas a separate account analyzes 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a phonetic role. The available evidence does not adjudicate these accounts or establish 同 as a sound component.

uncertainties.text: The bucket interpretation is a reported paleographic analysis, not a form independently checked here. The dossier does not identify the pictured object's spoken name, so the proposed borrowing of the graph for ‘put into effect/use’ has no independently established sound match; the pronunciations of 用 itself cannot supply that missing name.

Oracle-bone examples support an early use of 用 for whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense remain unresolved. A Qin-slip use read 桶 in a container or measure context does not settle their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This is an attested early use of the graph, not proof that it was the graph's original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶 in a container or measure sense. It preserves a container-related use but does not establish that this was the graph's original meaning or when it arose.

senses.gloss: prepositional use equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples are reported with prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb ‘use’. Their relative chronology and development are not established by the cited examples.
The character is used with the common meaning ‘use’ or ‘employ’. The supplied evidence does not establish a complete path from the inscriptional uses to the current range.

limitations.text: The sources attest several uses, but do not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘carry out/use’ remains unverified phonetically because the object's spoken name is not known.

overview.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One proposed account sees its ancient graph as a handled container reused for a similar-sounding word, but the object's name and sound match have not been established.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled container. Its proposed connection to ‘use’ depends on an unverified sound-based borrowing account.
